intent: One toggle button of a ToggleGroup, pressed when the group's value holds this item's value.
typical_uses: One option in a ToggleGroup's set of related toggle buttons

dont_use_when.situation: A single on/off control with no group around it

invariants.text: Inside a ToggleGroup the item is pressed exactly when the group's value array contains this item's `value`; the item's own `pressed` and `defaultPressed` are ignored there.

`value` is the string the group's value array records for this item. The types leave it optional, but without it the item falls back to a generated id, and a group whose `value` or `defaultValue` is set reports a development-mode error for the item.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a ToggleGroupItem outside a ToggleGroup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use Toggle for a standalone control; outside a group the item has no shared value to join, and its own `variant` and `size` are ignored in favour of the defaults

anti_patterns.dont: Leave an icon-only item with no aria-label
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label` naming the option the glyph stands for

a11y.by: The primitive's Toggle (a native button carrying aria-pressed bound to the pressed state) plus toggle-group.test.tsx's getByRole('button', { name }) and data-pressed assertions on aria-labelled items

value.states: value is typed by the caller's own Value type parameter, not a plain string
value.because: `ToggleGroupItemProps<Value extends string = string>` lets a caller narrow the value to its own literal union, the same one the group's value array holds; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so only its base shape is asserted and the narrowing is checked by tsc.

onPressedChange.states: onPressedChange is a callback of the next pressed state and event details, called before the group commits its change
onPressedChange.because: Base UI types it as `(pressed: boolean, eventDetails) => void`, and cancelling through eventDetails there also vetoes the group's value change; a function has no JSON Schema representation, so nothing beyond its presence is asserted.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the item's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (pressed, disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through toggle-group.module.css and the Toggle classes, not through this.

good.title: An icon-only item named for assistive tech
good.code:
<ToggleGroup aria-label="Alignment">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="left" iconOnly aria-label="Align left"><AlignLeftIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="right" iconOnly aria-label="Align right"><AlignRightIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>

bad.title: Pressed state set on the item instead of the group
bad.code:
<ToggleGroup aria-label="View">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="list" pressed aria-label="List"><ListIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="grid" aria-label="Grid"><GridIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
bad.why: Inside a group the item's `pressed` is ignored; set the group's `value` or `defaultValue` to `['list']` instead.

onPressedChange.description: TS: ((pressed: boolean, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element | undefined; }) => void) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. onPressedChange is a callback of the next pressed state and event details, called before the group commits its change. Base UI types it as `(pressed: boolean, eventDetails) => void`, and cancelling through eventDetails there also vetoes the group's value change; a function has no JSON Schema representation, so nothing beyond its presence is asserted.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ToggleState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ToggleState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the item's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (pressed, disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through toggle-group.module.css and the Toggle classes, not through this.

value.description: TS: Value | undefined. Not fully expressible in JSON Schema; what the type states beyond the kind above is checked by tsc. value is typed by the caller's own Value type parameter, not a plain string. `ToggleGroupItemProps<Value extends string = string>` lets a caller narrow the value to its own literal union, the same one the group's value array holds; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so only its base shape is asserted and the narrowing is checked by tsc.
